items.title: FIGHT/REMATCH button looks tappable but is a countdown
items.what: In the pre-fight screen (screenshot 2) and post-fight screen (screenshot 8), the large gold 'FIGHT' and 'REMATCH' buttons have a dark countdown circle inside them (e.g., '2' and '8'). The gold button styling makes it look like an active, tappable control.
items.why: A player's first instinct is to tap the button to start the match or rematch. When tapping does nothing because it's just a countdown, it feels broken and creates friction at the most critical moment.
items.how: Either make the countdown a separate element from the button (e.g., a countdown number floating above the button), or grey out the button during the countdown, or make the button actually tappable to skip the countdown.

items.title: Fighters are small and sit low, leaving dead space above
items.what: In screenshots 3 and 13, the two fighters are rendered in the lower-middle of the frame, with a large amount of empty dojo backdrop above them. The fighters are roughly 30% of the screen height.
items.why: The action feels distant and less impactful. On a phone, the player's attention is drawn to the center, but the fight is happening in the lower half, making it harder to track the characters and read the action.
items.how: Zoom the camera in to make the fighters larger, and/or shift the camera up so the fighters are more vertically centered. Alternatively, reduce the vertical dead space by making the dojo backdrop less empty.

items.title: Directional arrows on the STANCE and TECHNIQUE sticks are hard to see
items.what: In screenshots 3, 4, and 13, the arrows on the two large circular controls are thin grey glyphs on a dark background. The central dots are small and colored (blue/yellow).
items.why: The player needs to instantly understand which direction is 'step' or 'jump'. Low contrast arrows make the controls illegible in the game's dark, warm lighting, especially on a phone with glare or in a bright room.
items.how: Increase the brightness of the arrows (e.g., a lighter grey or gold), make them thicker, or add a subtle glow behind them. The 'High contrast' setting should also increase the arrow visibility.

items.title: MOVES and settings buttons are too small to tap reliably
items.what: In screenshot 3, the 'MOVES' button and the settings gear in the top-right are about 30px tall. The 'MOVES' button is a small rectangle and the gear is a small circle.
items.why: On a 390px-wide portrait phone, the recommended minimum touch target is 44x44px. These buttons are below that, leading to missed taps and frustration, especially during a fight.
items.how: Increase the size of both buttons to at least 44x44px, increase the padding around the icons, and consider moving them slightly down from the status bar.

items.title: TECHNIQUES list is too small and dense to read on a phone
items.what: In screenshot 6, the move list uses small text (~12px) and small icons for the stick inputs. The rows are tightly packed with little separation.
items.why: The player needs to read the move names and understand the inputs. On a phone, this small text is hard to read and the dense layout makes it easy to accidentally tap the wrong row.
items.how: Increase the font size and row height, and enlarge the input icons. Make the modal full-screen or use a larger scrollable area so the text is comfortably readable.
